extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in CBS News (media history, personnel, controversies, and partnerships)
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of CBS News covering current and past personnel, reporting partnerships, organizational leadership, controversies, and notable events. Useful for readers seeking factual and historical information about the network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content‑sharing agreement objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Content‑sharing agreements include the ability to share resources, footage, and reports, and conduct "efficient planning of news gathering resources to increase the content of each broadcaster's coverage of world events" (example: 2017 BBC partnership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships should enable resource/footage/report sharing and more efficient planning to expand world-coverage content; cited as replacing prior BBC/ABC/Sky arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and sources must be properly verified — the 2004 Killian documents controversy involved Dan Rather presenting improperly verified documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing or broadcasting documents without adequate authentication; the controversy prompted scrutiny and procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic work must avoid plagiarism — CBS has faced accusations of plagiarism and responded by firing producers and revamping procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear sourcing and attribution; plagiarism incidents have led to personnel actions and process changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate attribution and representation of footage
rubrics_metrics.description: Footage must not be misrepresented or erroneously attributed — there have been several instances cited of misrepresented or erroneously attributed footage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure location/timing/source of footage is accurate and clearly attributed to avoid public corrections and reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain editorial/journalistic independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial independence should be preserved; departures (e.g., Bill Owens) were attributed to a loss of journalistic independence under ownership/editorial changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structures and practices should protect newsroom independence from owners' editorial interventions or perceived interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perceived political bias / preserve impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid both accusations of liberal bias and perceptions of conservative/pro‑Trump bias; examples include historic accusations of liberal bias and later allegations of pro‑Trump bias under new leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for impartial reporting; be cautious of practices (guest selection, framing) that can create perceptions of bias or false balance (example: January 6 coverage criticism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles for news presentation ('5 simple values')
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs may adopt explicit guiding principles that inform how news is presented — example: Tony Dokoupil introduced '5 simple values' described as espousing American‑centric values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public articulation of guiding values can shape editorial choices but may also generate public debate about intent and neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about relationships with political figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency is required to avoid perceptions of coziness between a news organization and political actors — attendance at events 'honoring' political figures raised concerns about perception of closeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose and consider optics of staff/leadership attendance at political events; such actions can undermine trust or raise conflict‑of‑interest concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care in hiring contributors to avoid promoting misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring contributors with contested or fringe views (e.g., those associated with 'functional medicine' or labeled 'germ theory denialist') risks misinforming audiences on subject matter like health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet contributors' public record and expertise; balance platforming voices with potential to spread unproven claims, especially on scientific/health topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ombudsman role and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: An ombudsman or similar oversight role may be used to address perceived bias or standards — proposals to 'install an ombudsman to root out bias' and notes that a new ombudsman's duties may differ from the traditional definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ombudsman duties clearly and maintain independence for credibility; changes to the role can affect public trust in standards enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce/union and labor considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor actions and staff treatment are part of organizational standards — examples include streaming workers' walkouts and tentative contract deals, as well as reports of layoffs and who they affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat staff fairly during restructures; consider impacts on diversity and newsroom morale, as mass layoffs and perceived discriminatory cuts have prompted criticism and coverage.
